import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 599

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/599](https://www.erdosproblems.com/599)
- [AhBe09] Aharoni, Ron and Berger, Eli, *Menger's theorem for infinite graphs*,
  *Invent. Math.* **176** (2009), 1--62.
-/

open SimpleGraph

namespace Erdos599

/--
**Erdős Problem 599** (the Erdős–Menger conjecture).

Let $G$ be a (possibly infinite) graph and let $A, B$ be disjoint independent sets of
vertices. Must there exist a family $P$ of pairwise vertex-disjoint paths from $A$ to $B$,
and a set $S$ of vertices containing exactly one vertex from each path in $P$, such that
every path from $A$ to $B$ contains at least one vertex of $S$?

For finite $G$ this is equivalent to Menger's theorem. The answer is **yes**, proved by
Aharoni and Berger [AhBe09].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_599 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V) (A B : Set V),
      Disjoint A B → G.IsIndepSet A → G.IsIndepSet B →
      ∃ (ι : Type) (a b : ι → V) (p : ∀ i, G.Walk (a i) (b i)) (S : Set V),
        (∀ i, a i ∈ A) ∧ (∀ i, b i ∈ B) ∧ (∀ i, (p i).IsPath) ∧
        (Pairwise fun i j => Disjoint {v | v ∈ (p i).support} {v | v ∈ (p j).support}) ∧
        S ⊆ {v | ∃ i, v ∈ (p i).support} ∧
        (∀ i, ∃! v, v ∈ S ∧ v ∈ (p i).support) ∧
        (∀ a' ∈ A, ∀ b' ∈ B, ∀ q : G.Walk a' b', q.IsPath → ∃ v ∈ q.support, v ∈ S) := by
  sorry

/--
**Menger's theorem for infinite graphs** (Aharoni–Berger [AhBe09]).

The theorem actually proved by Aharoni and Berger holds for arbitrary vertex sets $A$
and $B$: in any (possibly infinite) graph $G$ there is a family $P$ of pairwise
vertex-disjoint $A$--$B$ paths together with an $A$--$B$ separator $S$ consisting of the
choice of exactly one vertex from each path in $P$. The disjointness and independence
hypotheses of `erdos_599` are not needed.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_599.variants.aharoni_berger :
    ∀ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V) (A B : Set V),
      ∃ (ι : Type) (a b : ι → V) (p : ∀ i, G.Walk (a i) (b i)) (S : Set V),
        (∀ i, a i ∈ A) ∧ (∀ i, b i ∈ B) ∧ (∀ i, (p i).IsPath) ∧
        (Pairwise fun i j => Disjoint {v | v ∈ (p i).support} {v | v ∈ (p j).support}) ∧
        S ⊆ {v | ∃ i, v ∈ (p i).support} ∧
        (∀ i, ∃! v, v ∈ S ∧ v ∈ (p i).support) ∧
        (∀ a' ∈ A, ∀ b' ∈ B, ∀ q : G.Walk a' b', q.IsPath → ∃ v ∈ q.support, v ∈ S) := by
  sorry

/--
Sanity check: when $A = \varnothing$ the conclusion of `erdos_599` holds trivially, with
the empty family of paths and $S = \varnothing$ (the covering condition is vacuous since
there is no path starting in $\varnothing$).
-/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_599.test.empty_A (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V) (B : Set V) :
    ∃ (ι : Type) (a b : ι → V) (p : ∀ i, G.Walk (a i) (b i)) (S : Set V),
      (∀ i, a i ∈ (∅ : Set V)) ∧ (∀ i, b i ∈ B) ∧ (∀ i, (p i).IsPath) ∧
      (Pairwise fun i j => Disjoint {v | v ∈ (p i).support} {v | v ∈ (p j).support}) ∧
      S ⊆ {v | ∃ i, v ∈ (p i).support} ∧
      (∀ i, ∃! v, v ∈ S ∧ v ∈ (p i).support) ∧
      (∀ a' ∈ (∅ : Set V), ∀ b' ∈ B, ∀ q : G.Walk a' b', q.IsPath →
        ∃ v ∈ q.support, v ∈ S) := by
  refine ⟨Empty, Empty.elim, Empty.elim, fun i => i.elim, ∅,
    fun i => i.elim, fun i => i.elim, fun i => i.elim, fun i => i.elim,
    fun v hv => hv.elim, fun i => i.elim, fun a' ha' => absurd ha' (Set.notMem_empty _)⟩

end Erdos599

reformulations.difference: The main theorem assumes disjoint independent terminal sets, whereas the unrestricted-set undirected form of Aharoni–Berger, stated in the file's variant, allows arbitrary terminal sets.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: These universal undirected-graph statements are equivalent. To obtain the unrestricted version, reserve every vertex of A ∩ B as a singleton path and remove those vertices. Delete edges internal to either remaining terminal set, making the sets independent. Apply the restricted statement. Every original A–B path avoiding A ∩ B contains an A–B subpath with no internal terminal vertices, so that subpath survives the edge deletions and meets the resulting separator. Restore the reserved singleton paths and add A ∩ B to the separator. The reverse implication is immediate.

reformulations.difference: Instead of explicitly making S the image of a function choosing one vertex from each path, Lean requires S to be contained in the union of the supports and to meet each support in exactly one vertex. The main theorem uses the same encoding.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For pairwise disjoint supports Wᵢ, these conditions are equivalent to existence of f with f(i) ∈ Wᵢ and S = Set.range f. Forward, choose each unique intersection vertex; the subset condition excludes additional elements of S. Conversely, disjointness prevents a choice from another path from creating a second intersection. The full conclusion-equivalence was proved as Review599.conclusion_iff_chosen in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, without using the conjecture's sorry proofs.

sources_consulted: Aharoni–Berger, Menger's theorem for infinite graphs, arXiv:math/0509397v4: Theorem 1.6, Definition 1.3, and §2.3; LaTeX source at https://arxiv.org/e-print/math/0509397v4
Local Mathlib sources: Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/Basic.lean, Walk/Basic.lean, Paths.lean, Clique.lean; Logic/Pairwise.lean; Data/Set/Disjoint.lean.
review.notes: Checked all three declarations. The primary paper proves the stronger directed-graph theorem; the variant accurately states its undirected specialization. Lean checks confirmed singleton paths, A ∩ B ⊆ S, injectivity of path starting vertices, separation by paths versus walks, and the empty-set, edgeless-graph, equal-terminal-set, and single-edge cases. The existing empty_A proof has no sorry dependency. The final scratch file compiled successfully, and the reviewed file was unchanged. Direct access to erdosproblems.com/599 remained blocked by Cloudflare despite descriptive User-Agent headers; its exact live prose and remarks were unavailable. Mathematical comparison used the cited primary paper, and the community database independently confirmed the affirmative solved status.
